findings.criterion: Medium: reduces clarity or creates inconsistent understanding
findings.before: **\[ANALYSIS\] Token economy.** Markdown's syntactic overhead is low relative to tag-based formats. `**bold**` is 8 characters / a few tokens; `bold` is 21 characters and more tokens; a styled HTML equivalent is worse. Across a long response, Markdown leaves more of the token budget for content. This is a plausible and arithmetically sound advantage, though it is rarely the *stated* design driver.
findings.after: **\[ANALYSIS\] Token economy.** Markdown can express the same formatting with fewer characters than tag-based HTML: `**bold**` is 8 characters, while `bold` is 21. Token counts depend on the tokenizer and surrounding text, so this character comparison does not measure a token saving. Compare complete outputs with the intended model's tokenizer before assigning a budget benefit. Compact markup remains a plausible adoption mechanism, rather than a measured cause here.
findings.reason: Character counts do not establish tokenizer-dependent token counts or a measured budget advantage.
